chunks: Say: 'I seek refuge with the Lord of men.'
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to seek refuge with the Lord of men in Surah An-Nas?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often recited alongside Surah Al-Falaq as part of the *Mu'awwidhatayn*, emphasizing the necessity of seeking refuge in Allah's absolute sovereignty (*Rububiyyah*) to ward off the subtle whispers (*Waswasa*) of Satan and human allies. It underscores the theological principle that true protection comes not from mere invocation, but from recognizing the Lord who nurtures and sustains all mankind, a concept deeply linked to the Imams' role as guides who help believers navigate spiritual trials.
